anchor_source.source: AEO2025 reference case, EMM Northeast Power Coordinating Council / New England

standing_caveats: AEO EMM regions approximate ISO footprints (each anchor row's own note); region rows were summed to ISO totals with the loader's extensive-quantity rule.

D14 measured the shared economic exit screen at recall 2/6 with a gas-concentration bias on the NEISO crossover window (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d14-neiso-t1x-2026-08-30.md §2); every model-side fleet composition row inherits it.
AEO2025 reference froze law as of Dec 2024 (pre-OBBBA, CAA §111 in force), so its coal exit path is regulatory-assumption-heavy and its offshore-wind pipeline predates 2025-26 procurement turbulence.

GENERATION FAMILY NEWLY DISPOSITIONED (D29): the summary now carries generation_by_fuel_mwh, so the six AEO generation series are dispositioned for the first time; model in-region generation nets out the 'import' pseudo-fuel (~30-33 TWh interchange). The pre-R-A table's caveat 4 (generation not dispositionable) is dissolved.

STORAGE COLUMN NOW REAL (D29): storage rows read storage_power_mw with the 1,865.0 MW NEISO pumped-storage residual netted out for the battery-only AEO 'Diurnal Storage' comparison; capacity:pumped_storage is dispositioned as its own row. The pre-R-A caveat 5 is dissolved.

This table dispositions the ARMED-posture golden (storage_entry gates true, owner ruling R-A); the prior (pre-R-A) table is preserved at results/ff-corridor/dispositions/neiso-t3-prera-2026-08-31.json.

rows.anchor_basis: AEO Total Capacity (region-summed; includes PS + diurnal storage)
rows.explanation: The total-row deficit closes as the sum of this table's own named component gaps: offshore wind -6.40 GW (wind_total row), diurnal storage -0.99 GW (storage row), and the CT capacity AEO adds that the model's economic entry (2031+ only in this solve) has not yet built — partly offset by +1.1 GW solar overshoot and +1.7 GW retained oil-steam. No residual is unaccounted (D25 §4.3 mechanism 10, re-summed on this bundle; the PS leg of the pre-R-A explanation dissolves — storage_power_mw now carries PS inside the model total).

gas_cc + gas_cc_ccs
gas_ct + gas_st + oil (one block vs AEO CT + Fossil Steam)
rows.anchor_basis: AEO Combustion Turbine/Diesel + Fossil Steam (= oil + gas steam)

rows.model_basis: capacity_by_fuel_mw[nuclear]
capacity_by_fuel_mw[hydro]
capacity_by_fuel_mw[solar]
rows.explanation: ACP-pinned RPS dual redirects the model's clean build into utility PV: this bundle's rps_dual sits at the $50 ACP ceiling in every committed year, and the entry machinery answers the RPS with the cheapest eligible VRE (solar, in the anti-cobweb 1,802/1,198 MW alternating cadence) while AEO satisfies the same policy with OSW. Mechanisms 3 and 4 are one divergence seen from opposite sides (D25 §4.3), re-measured on this bundle.

rows.model_basis: generic wind (model carries no onshore/offshore split)
rows.explanation: No state-procurement build channel for offshore wind: OSW is an available entry tech (offshore_wind_available_year=2030) that the merchant CONE screen never selects in this bundle through 2050; AEO carries the contracted New England OREC pipeline (6.40 GW by 2030, 8.54 by 2040). The divergence is which instrument builds clean capacity — procurement (theirs, unrepresented) vs merchant screen + capped RPS (ours). D25 §4.3 mechanism 3, re-measured on this bundle.

rows.model_basis: storage_power_mw - 1,865.0 MW PS residual (battery-only, per the D29 classification note)
rows.anchor_basis: AEO Diurnal Storage (batteries only; AEO books PS separately)
rows.explanation: Zero storage entry through 2049 UNDER THE ARMED POSTURE (run_config: storage_entry_availability_gate=true, storage_entry_cost_normalized_rank=true — owner ruling R-A), so the battery fleet at this anchor is still the 0.77 GW EIA-860 base and the -56.2 % divergence is UNCHANGED by the arming — itself a measured campaign result (T3-GOLDEN-2 finding §6). RE-AUTHORED per D36 §7 to name the driver, which the prior wording ('the value stack clears no tech') did not. THE DRIVER — PROCUREMENT CHANNEL UNREPRESENTED, the same instrument family as the offshore-wind rows (D25 §4.3 mechanism 3): AEO2025 carries New England's storage procurement obligations as policy inputs (the Massachusetts 2024 climate statute's 5,000 MW storage directive by 2030, Connecticut Public Act 21-53's 1,000 MW storage target, the MA Clean Peak Energy Standard credit stream — each an enforceable public instrument to be confirmed at intake, and each formulaic in the rule-13 sense: a dated MW obligation, not a fitted quantity); the model builds storage only through the merchant economic screen, so a contracted MW obligation has no way in. Were that channel ever chartered it would enter as a known-additions row (step 4), never through the screen. THE MODEL-SIDE RESIDUAL (R-1) — the merchant stack's own arbitrage blindness: D36 reconstructs the value stack year by year and finds the arbitrage leg the SHORT TERM IN EVERY YEAR by $50-150/kW-yr, with the RA leg second-order (and D33's, not a second storage mechanism). With the RA leg at its maximum AND the arbitrage leg at the real ISO-NE market's best year, li-ion 4 h is short in every year — a faithful merchant arbitrage-plus-FCA stack does not build 1.76 GW of New England batteries by 2030 on this cost basis. The screen's price object is a static re-price of the entering year's zonal duals that carries neither the tail nor the trough; the identified route is the GATED default-OFF entry_forward_expectation_signal (NEISO cell U), an entry-signal mechanism that moves every capacity screen rather than a storage one (rule 19), and its zero-cost precondition is entry_screen_diagnostics on the next NEISO solve. THE HORIZON'S SOLE ENTRY — 720 MW of 100-h iron_air in 2050 (evolution_2050.json; 0.6 tech-share cap x 1,200 MW NEISO annual cap; no second tech claims the remaining 480 MW) — falls after the anchor window and is a DATA-channel result: the RC-R demand-curve intake's re-timed exits tighten the 2049-2050 stack. It is NOT a D-3-rank result; D-3 is sign-preserving and chose among clearers, of which iron-air was the only one (D36 §1, §4). AEO carries ~1.0 GW more diurnal storage by 2030; the corridor number is context, never a target (rule 13). Source: D36 §7 (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d36-storage-valuestack-2026-09-02.md), routed §8 item 1; re-authored by D38, 2026-09-02.

rows.anchor_basis: AEO Wood and Other Biomass + Municipal Waste
rows.explanation: Sector-boundary basis: AEO's Electric Power Sector capacity excludes end-use/CHP wood; the model fleet is the EIA-860 grid registry including IPP/CHP units. Documented basis mismatch on a class ~2 % of fleet (D25 §4.3 mechanism 9, unchanged).

rows.model_basis: trajectory co2_mt (dispatch x per-generator emission rates)
rows.explanation: The 45Q + resolved-RGGI CCS retrofit wave: the spec-§5.6 screen converts the CC fleet at its 3 GW/yr cap from 2028 (this bundle: 8,998 MW gas_cc_ccs by 2030) under the 45Q window (ira_ccus_45q_last_year=2032) plus the resolved RGGI escalator ($26.05/t 2026 -> $132.16/t 2050, D23 §2; carbon_price field 0.0, program-resolved). AEO also carries RGGI at a far lower allowance path and retrofits nothing. Model CO2 at 2030 is HIGHER (+60 %): the model's renewable fleet is ~19 TWh smaller (the OSW procurement gap, generation:renewables row) and its retained oil/CT + unabated CC still dispatch pre-conversion, while AEO's larger VRE fleet displaces gas early.

rows.model_basis: total_gen_mwh - generation_by_fuel_mwh[import] (imports are interchange, not in-region generation)
generation_by_fuel_mwh[coal]
gas_cc + gas_cc_ccs + gas_ct + gas_st generation
rows.anchor_basis: AEO Natural Gas generation (all gas cycles)
rows.explanation: The OSW procurement gap seen in energy space, plus the model's CCS-heavy dispatch: AEO's contracted OSW fleet (6.4-8.5 GW) generates the bulk of its 46-73 TWh renewables block, displacing gas; the model has no procurement channel (wind_total row), so gas-CCS dispatch (23.1 TWh of the 36.2 TWh gas total at 2030 is abated gas_cc_ccs) and imports back-fill the missing OSW energy. Same instrument divergence as mechanisms 3/4, expressed in generation.

rows.model_basis: generation_by_fuel_mwh[nuclear]
generation_by_fuel_mwh[oil]
rows.explanation: Both sides ~0 (< 0.02 TWh — the anchor is 8-12 GWh, roughly one afternoon of one peaker): a ratio on a near-zero denominator manufactures the percentage, so the divergence is explained as a level-scale artifact — model and AEO agree that NEISO oil-fired ENERGY is essentially zero even while the oil CAPACITY rows differ (the fleet is retained for capacity value, not dispatched).

rows.model_basis: wind + solar + hydro + biomass dispatched energy (post-curtailment)
rows.anchor_basis: AEO Renewable Sources generation (incl. conventional hydro)
rows.explanation: The renewables-generation shortfall is the OSW energy gap: model wind+solar+hydro+biomass dispatched energy vs AEO's renewable block that embeds the OREC pipeline's offshore output. The model's PV overshoot (solar row) recovers part of it by 2040 but cannot close a 6-8.5 GW offshore fleet's energy. Mechanism 3 in energy space; post-curtailment dispatch is quoted (I3's out-year dump starts 2043, after these anchors).
